heroSection.title: Benefit Discounts
heroSection.subTitle: Benefits-First Discount Directory
heroSection.description: A public directory of the discounts companies offer to people on federal financial support programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, or more. Pick the benefits you actually hold and the list narrows to what is open to you, with every entry linked to the operator's own page.

mainContent.overview: Built and launched a public directory of the discounts that private companies, state governments, and cultural institutions offer to people on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, and similar benefit programs. Readers pick the benefits they hold and the list narrows to matching offers, with state, category, and keyword filters on top. Every entry links to the operator's own page and shows the last time it was checked, while a weekly sweep re-reads each source page to catch offers that have changed. The site never calculates eligibility, never collects anything from readers, and carries no affiliate links. Built with Next.js and Postgres on Vercel.

keyFeature.body: Pick the benefits you actually hold, such as SNAP, Medicaid, or other benefit programs, and the list narrows to the offers open to you. Choose your state and each benefit appears under the name your state uses for it, with category and keyword filters layered on top

Discounts and assistance programs from private companies, state governments and cultural institutions, gathered into a single searchable list instead of sitting scattered across separate company pages that rarely link to one another

Every entry shows the last time it was checked, and a weekly sweep re-reads each source page after that. If a page has changed since the last check, its entry says so, and a page that cannot be read automatically is labeled plainly instead of left looking current
Every entry links to the company's own page for that offer, so you are always one click from the authoritative terms instead of a summary that may have drifted out of date
The site never calculates whether you qualify, never asks for a document, photo, or form, and carries no affiliate links anywhere. It shows what the company itself says and leaves the decision to you

No account, no sign-up, and nothing collected about you. Your filters stay in your own browser and are kept out of the address bar, and you can save them on your device or share a filtered view whenever you choose

walkthrough.subheader: Pick what you hold, see what is open
walkthrough.description: The directory is organized by benefit, location, and category. One control card asks where you live, what you have, and what you want it to cover, and the list narrows as you answer. Search also matches participating companies and locations, and results sort by name, company, last checked, or date added. The whole list is pre-rendered, so it loads fast and stays readable even with JavaScript turned off.

walkthrough.subheader: Everything about one offer on one page
walkthrough.description: Each program gets its own page with the full benefit detail, a link to the official page, and the last time it was checked. Benefits show the name your state uses for them, and programs that run through many venues, such as museum admission, providing a location url for every participating location. The page also reports what the weekly sweep found, whether nothing has changed, the page has changed, or it cannot be read automatically.

walkthrough.subheader: A queue of what needs checking next
walkthrough.description: A GitHub login restricted to approved email addresses opens a queue sorted by what was checked longest ago, with a column that flags pages that changed since they were last verified. Marking an entry verified takes one click, and every field is validated before it saves. The panel also downloads a full backup, restores one after checking every row, and adds new programs from a file without overwriting existing ones.
